exposure: pH on blood-gas analysis after HHFNC application
pCO2 on blood-gas analysis after HHFNC application
Incidence of respiratory distress syndrome of newborn (RDS)
outcome: Treatment failure of HHFNC (requiring other respiratory support due to respiratory acidosis, hypoxia, or apnea)
cohort: 97 newborns who required non-invasive respiratory support within 24 hours after birth.
finding: Newborns of less than 34 weeks, infants with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), higher FiO2 settings during HHFNC, and post-HHFNC acidosis and hypercarbia were identified as significant risk factors for HHFNC treatment failure.
gest_age: Varied, with specific analysis for less than 34 weeks, and failure rates provided for >=33 weeks, >=34 weeks, and >=36 weeks.
